newsitem.title: UK: Brent physical cargo trades at lower level.
newsitem.headline: Brent physical cargo trades at lower level.

text.p: A cargo of physical Brent crude traded on Wednesday seven cents below Tuesday's traded level.
A major bought a February 26-28 cargo at March Brent +5 cents - down from a +12 cent deal on Tuesday for a February 22-24 loader, traders said.
This cargo was additional to the original programme, equity holders said, and was heard destined for Eastern Europe.

Few buyers were seen for the remaining three February loading cargoes and one seller was offering at March +5 cents - down from an early offer at +15 cents. March Brent on the IPE lost some 23 cents to trade at $20.91 a barrel by 1250 GMT.
Brent equity holders expected the March loading programme to be released on Thursday. The programme was not expected to hold many surprises.
"It'll just be up a bit because of the longer month," one equity holder said.

The cargo which was defered on Tuesday was offered by a trader as a Feb 27-Mar 01 loader. The only other Brent cargo which might be available was a Feb 26-28 cargo which was not as yet being actively offered, traders said.
Talk of Gullfaks and Oseberg trades on Tuesday could not be immediately confirmed.

In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals was steady around -90 cents a barrel cif Genoa as the impact of loading delays at the Black Sea port of Novorossiisk balanced slack spot demand from refiners, traders said.
"There's basically been very little change since yesterday," said one.
Novorossiisk remained shut on Wednesday because of high winds and swell after reopening for only three hours on Tuesday.
Traders said some Med refiners were eyeing North Sea barrels as margins for regional crudes remain thin.
